examples.ko: 제 동생은 프로 게이머가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling wants to become a pro gamer.
Gamers wait for new games to come out.
This chair is popular with gamers.

examples.ko: 저도 게이머라서 게임 소식을 자주 봐요.
examples.en: I'm a gamer too, so I often check game news.
I met a famous gamer in person.

examples.ko: 우리 반에는 게이머 친구가 세 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are three gamer friends in our class.

explain: 게임을 직업으로 하는 사람은 '프로 게이머'라고 해요. 취미로 즐기는 사람은 그냥 '게이머'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My older brother is a famous pro gamer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임을 직업으로 하는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to someone who plays games as a job.

phrases.example: 게이머들이 새 게임을 사려고 줄을 섰어요.
phrases.en: Gamers lined up to buy the new game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 명일 때 '-들'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-들' when talking about several gamers.

phrases.en: I am a person who plays games.
phrases.nuance_ko: '게이머'를 쉬운 말로 풀어 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain way to explain what a gamer is.

explain_en: Someone who plays games as a job is a 프로 게이머. Someone who plays for fun is simply a 게이머.

examples.en: You board the plane at gate 12.
An announcement said the gate had changed.
I wait for my friend in front of the gate.
I tapped my card at the subway gate and went in.
I arrived before the boarding gate closed.
A new security gate appeared at the entrance.

explain: 공항에서는 '탑승구'와 같은 곳을 가리켜요. 역이나 건물 출입구에도 쓰는 외래어예요. '정문'이나 '입구'라고 하는 큰 문은 보통 게이트라고 하지 않아요.

phrases.en: Please wait in front of the boarding gate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비행기를 타는 문을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The gate where you board the plane.

phrases.en: Did you check the gate number?
phrases.nuance_ko: 공항에서 번호를 확인할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used at the airport when checking numbers.

phrases.en: Let's meet in front of the gate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만날 장소를 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to set a meeting place.

explain_en: At an airport, it points to the same place as '탑승구'. It is a loanword also used for station and building entrances. A main front door called '정문' or '입구' is usually not called a gate.

examples.ko: 너무 힘들어서 회사를 관둘까 생각 중이에요.
examples.en: It is so hard that I am thinking about quitting my job.
My younger sibling quit the academy they were attending.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 아르바이트를 관두고 여행을 갈 거예요.
examples.en: Next month I will quit my part-time job and go traveling.
If you don't want to do it, it's fine to quit now.
I told the manager the reason I am quitting.
I never give up halfway.

explain: '그만두다'를 줄여서 말할 때 쓰는 형태예요. 편하게 말할 때 쓰고, 윗사람에게 하는 말이나 글에서는 '그만두다'가 더 알맞아요. '관둬요', '관뒀어요'처럼 '둬'로 바뀌는 활용에 주의하세요.

phrases.en: I have too much work, so I want to quit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그만하고 싶은 마음을 말할 때 쓰는 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say you want to stop or quit.

phrases.en: If it's hard, just quit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '관두다'의 해요체 활용이에요. '관두어요'가 아니라 '관둬요'로 줄여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The 해요체 form of 관두다; it contracts to 관둬요, not 관두어요.

phrases.en: I am quitting my job next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '관두다'의 원래 말이에요. 윗사람에게 말하거나 글에서는 이 말이 더 알맞아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of 관두다; better for elders or writing.

explain_en: It is the shortened form of '그만두다' used in casual speech. With superiors or in writing, '그만두다' fits better. Watch the conjugation, which changes to '둬': '관둬요', '관뒀어요'.

dis.h: casual quit; give up for good

p.n: Using the other word for quitting a job is unnatural; it is used for stopping an activity.

examples.ko: 급행열차를 타면 서울까지 한 시간 걸려요.
examples.en: If you take the express train, it takes an hour to Seoul.
The express train doesn't stop at small stations.

examples.ko: 급행열차가 오기 전에 표를 사야 해요.
examples.en: We have to buy tickets before the express train arrives.

examples.ko: 급행열차 대신 완행열차를 타고 천천히 갔어요.
examples.en: I took a slow train instead of the express and went leisurely.
There were almost no seats on the express train.
To transfer to the express train, get off at the next station.

explain: 반대말은 모든 역에 서는 '완행열차'예요. 말할 때는 그냥 '급행'이라고 줄여서 말하는 경우도 많고, 지하철에도 '급행'이 있어요. 빠른 대신 서는 역이 적어서 어느 역에 서는지 꼭 확인해야 해요.

phrases.en: If you take the express, you get there much faster.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급행열차'를 줄인 말로, 말할 때 더 자주 써요. 지하철에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form used more in speech, and also used for subways.

phrases.en: Which stations does the express train stop at?
phrases.nuance_ko: 서는 역이 적은 열차라서 정차 역을 물을 때 꼭 필요한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Since it stops at few stations, this is key for asking where it stops.
phrases.en_equiv: station where the express train stops

phrases.en: The local train stops at every station, so it is slow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급행열차'의 반대말이에요. 둘을 비교할 때 같이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of the express train, said together when comparing the two.

explain_en: Its opposite is '완행열차', which stops at every station. In speech people often shorten it to '급행', and subways have a '급행' too. It is faster but stops at fewer stations, so check which stations it stops at.

examples.en: My father had major surgery and is recovering.
I'm relieved the major surgery went well.
After major surgery you have to rest for a while.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 대수술까지는 필요 없다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said I don't need anything as big as major surgery.
I can't sleep with the major operation coming up.
This reorganization is a major overhaul of the company structure.

explain: 병원에서 쓰는 말이지만 제도나 조직을 크게 고칠 때 비유로도 자주 써요. '큰 수술'과 거의 같게 말하고, 반대는 '작은 수술'이에요.

phrases.en: My grandmother had major surgery.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대수술'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 대수술 and common in daily speech.

phrases.en: I had major surgery last year and got healthier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수술은 '받다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Surgery goes with the verb 받다.

phrases.en: Fortunately, the major surgery ended well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수술 결과를 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to report how the surgery went.

explain_en: It is a hospital word, but it is also often used figuratively for a big overhaul of a system or organization. It is nearly the same as '큰 수술', and the opposite is '작은 수술'.

examples.ko: 차를 탈 때는 뒷좌석에도 안전벨트를 매세요.
examples.en: When you ride in a car, wear a seat belt in the back seat too.
A young child is safer sitting in the back seat.
I put the heavy bag on the back seat first.

examples.ko: 이 차는 뒷좌석이 넓어서 오래 타도 편해요.
examples.en: This car has a spacious back seat, so it is comfortable even for long rides.
I left my umbrella in the back seat of the taxi.
My friends are singing happily in the back seat.

explain: 택시에서는 보통 뒷좌석에 앉고, 친한 사람이 운전하는 차에서는 앞의 '조수석'에 앉기도 해요. 뒷좌석도 안전벨트를 매라는 안내가 자주 나와요. 교실이나 버스의 뒤쪽 자리는 '뒷자리'를 써요.

phrases.en: If you sit in the back, you can't see well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차뿐 아니라 교실이나 버스의 뒤쪽 자리도 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Covers back seats in classrooms and buses, not only cars.

phrases.en: Please move the front seat forward a little.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒷좌석'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 뒷좌석.

phrases.en: Please open the back seat door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차의 뒷자리 쪽 문을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the door on the back seat side of a car.

explain_en: In a taxi people usually sit in the back seat, while in a friend's car you may sit up front in the '조수석' (passenger seat). Announcements often remind you to buckle up in the back seat too. For the back seats in a classroom or on a bus, use '뒷자리'.

examples.en: The rocket goes high into the sky.
They launch a rocket into space tomorrow.
The kids made paper rockets.
I watched the rocket launch on television.
Rocket fuel burns very fast.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 새로운 로켓을 개발하고 있어요.
examples.en: That company is developing a new rocket.

explain: '로켓'은 위성이나 우주선을 우주로 보내는 발사체에 주로 써요. 뉴스에서는 '우주 발사체'라는 말도 같이 써요. '로켓을 발사하다', '로켓이 발사되다'처럼 '발사'와 자주 나와요. 물을 넣어 날리는 '물로켓'이나 '종이 로켓' 같은 장난감도 있어요.

phrases.en: Scientists launch a new rocket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 로켓을 쏘아 올릴 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase when people launch a rocket.

phrases.en: The rocket was launched at ten in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 쏘았는지보다 로켓에 일어난 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on what happened to the rocket, not who launched it.

phrases.en: The kids fly water rockets on the playground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물을 넣어 날리는 장난감 로켓을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A toy rocket that flies using water.

explain_en: '로켓' is mostly used for the launch vehicle that carries satellites and spacecraft into space. News also uses '우주 발사체'. It often comes with '발사', as in '로켓을 발사하다' and '로켓이 발사되다'. There are also toys such as '물로켓' (water rocket) and '종이 로켓'.

en: to be chosen; to be selected

examples.ko: 이 노래가 우리 반 대표곡으로 선택됐어요.
examples.en: This song was chosen as our class signature song.

examples.ko: 최종 후보 세 명 중 한 명이 선택돼요.
examples.en: One of the three final candidates will be chosen.

examples.ko: 이번에 선택되지 않아도 다음 기회가 있어요.
examples.en: Even if you're not chosen this time, there's another chance.

examples.ko: 학생 대표로 선택되면 인사를 해야 해요.
examples.en: If you're chosen as the student representative, you have to give a speech.
A menu that has been selected can't be changed.

examples.ko: 제 그림이 전시회에 선택될 거라고 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard my painting will be chosen for the exhibition.

explain: '선택하다'는 내가 고르는 것이고, '선택되다'는 골라 주는 쪽에서 뽑아 준 상태예요. 사람이 뽑힐 때는 구어에서 '뽑히다'가 더 자연스러워요. 앱 화면에서는 '선택됨'이라는 표시로 자주 만나요.

phrases.en: I was chosen as the class representative.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 고를 때는 구어에서 '선택되다'보다 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For people being picked, it sounds more natural in speech than '선택되다'.

phrases.en: A text message goes to the people who were selected.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 '뽑힌'이라는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies a noun, adding the sense of 'picked'.

phrases.en: The menu that is selected on the screen is blue.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 있다'를 붙여 지금 선택된 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 있다' describes the currently selected state.

explain_en: '선택하다' is you choosing; '선택되다' is having been picked by the one choosing. When a person gets picked, spoken Korean more naturally says '뽑히다'. You often meet it on app screens as the label '선택됨'.

examples.en: A small rest area was built in the park.
While hiking, I drank water at a rest area.
The elderly gather at the village rest area and chat.

examples.ko: 이 쉼터는 누구나 무료로 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can use this rest area for free.
We looked for a rest area and went into the shade.
The rest area in the middle of the road was clean too.

explain: 공원, 산길, 도로 옆처럼 잠깐 쉬어 가도록 만든 곳에 써요. 건물 안에서 쉬는 공간은 '휴게실'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I rested a while at the rest area on the mountain path.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쉼터'와 '쉬다'가 같은 말뿌리라서 자연스럽게 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 쉼터 and 쉬다 share a root, so they pair naturally.
phrases.en_equiv: to rest at a rest area

phrases.en: There is a small rest area by the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기를 나타내는 말과 함께 장소를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with a size word to describe the place.

phrases.en: The city hall built a rest area in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉴 수 있는 곳을 새로 지을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for building a new place to rest.

explain_en: It is used for places made for a short rest, such as a park, a mountain trail, or the side of a road. A resting space inside a building is called 휴게실.

examples.en: How can your voice be this pretty?
Maybe it will rain tomorrow.
How are you so good at cooking?
Perhaps he has arrived by now.

examples.ko: 어쩜 말도 없이 그냥 가 버렸어요?
examples.en: How could he just leave without a word?

examples.ko: 어쩜 제 생각이 틀릴 수도 있어요.
examples.en: Maybe my thinking could be wrong.

explain: 어쩜은 '어쩌면'의 줄임말처럼 쓰여서 '아마 그럴지도 몰라요'라는 느낌을 줘요. '어쩜 이렇게 예쁠까'처럼 놀라거나 감탄할 때도 써요. 이때는 뒤에 '이렇게', '그렇게'가 자주 와요.

phrases.en: Perhaps it might snow tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어쩜'의 원래 말이고, 말할 때와 글에서 모두 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of '어쩜', natural in both speech and writing.

phrases.en: How can it be this delicious?
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 눈앞의 것에 놀라거나 감탄할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express amazement at something right in front of you.

phrases.en: How can you be so kind?
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대나 다른 사람의 모습에 감탄할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express admiration at another person's manner.

explain_en: 어쩜 works as a short form of '어쩌면' and gives the feeling of 'perhaps'. It is also used to express surprise or admiration, as in '어쩜 이렇게 예쁠까'. In that use, '이렇게' or '그렇게' often follows.

examples.en: Walking alone on a night road feels dangerous.
Don't play risky pranks.
The child was sitting on the railing, which looked dangerous.
The driving felt dangerous.

examples.ko: 그 계획은 조금 위험스러울 것 같아요.
examples.en: That plan seems a bit risky.
It looked dangerous, so I didn't go near it.

explain: '위험하다'는 사실로 위험한 것, '위험스럽다'는 위험해 보이거나 그렇게 느껴진다는 말이에요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '위험스러워요', '위험스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 말할 때는 '위험해 보여요'도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 눈이 오는 날 산길은 위험스러운 길이에요.
phrases.en: A mountain road on a snowy day is a dangerous-looking road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '위험스럽다'가 '위험스러운'으로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, 위험스럽다 changes to 위험스러운.

phrases.en: This ride isn't so dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험해 보이지 않는다고 부정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something does not seem dangerous.

phrases.en: That bridge looks a bit dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: '위험스럽다'와 비슷한데 말할 때 더 자연스럽고 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 위험스럽다 but more natural and easier in speech.

explain_en: The plain adjective states that something is actually dangerous, while this one says it looks or feels dangerous. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so the ending changes in forms like the polite present and the modifier. In speech, 'it looks dangerous' is also common.

en: to be taken advantage of; to be exploited (by someone)

examples.ko: 저는 친구에게 이용당한 것 같아서 슬퍼요.
examples.en: I feel sad because it seems my friend used me.

examples.ko: 그는 사람들에게 이용당해도 화를 내지 않았어요.
examples.en: He didn't get angry even when people used him.
If you do not want to be used by others, refuse clearly.
Very naive people get used easily.
I felt the company was using me, so I quit my job.
I read contracts carefully so I won't be taken advantage of.

explain: 남이 자기 이익을 위해 나를 쓴 불쾌한 경험을 말해요. 단순히 서비스를 쓰는 '이용하다'나 중립적인 '이용되다'와 달라요. '무시당하다', '사기당하다'처럼 '-당하다'가 붙은 말은 보통 나쁜 일에 써요.

phrases.en: I found out later that my friend had used me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 이미 나쁜 일을 겪었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense: you already went through the bad experience.

phrases.en: I don't want to be used by anyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶지 않다'로 원하지 않는 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-고 싶지 않다' expresses not wanting it to happen.
phrases.en_equiv: I don't want to be used

phrases.en: I feel like that person used me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '느낌이 들다'와 함께 쓰면 확실하지 않아도 그렇게 느낀다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '느낌이 들다', it means you feel that way even if you're not certain.

explain_en: It describes the unpleasant experience of being used by someone for their own benefit. It differs from plain '이용하다' (using a service) and the neutral '이용되다'. Verbs ending in '-당하다', like '무시당하다' and '사기당하다', are normally used for bad things.

examples.en: I move into a new apartment next month.
Our family moved in last week.
I went today to see the house I will move into.
I greeted the neighbor who just moved in.
Once the date is set, I want to move in right away.
The construction was delayed, so we could not move in.

explain: 입주하다는 새로 지은 아파트나 오피스텔처럼 새 건물에 들어갈 때 어울려요. 보통 집에서 집으로 옮길 때는 '이사하다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The residents' meeting is tomorrow evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 건물이나 단지에 들어와 사는 사람들을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The people who move into and live in a new building or complex.

phrases.en: The move-in date has been set for March 1st.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새집에 들어가는 날을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the day you move into a new home.

phrases.example: 내년 봄에 새 아파트에 입주할 예정이에요.
phrases.en: I plan to move into the new apartment next spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 들어갈 계획을 말할 때 '-(으)ㄹ 예정이다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -(으)ㄹ 예정이다 to talk about a planned move-in.

explain_en: Ipjuhada fits when you move into a newly built apartment or office-tel. When you just move from one home to another, 'isahada' sounds more natural.

examples.en: Many curious animals live in the jungle.
The explorers went into the jungle.
The jungle is hot and humid, so it's hard to walk.
The child likes movies set in the jungle.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 정글의 길이 진흙으로 변해요.
examples.en: When it rains, the jungle paths turn to mud.

examples.ko: 정글에서 길을 잃은 사람을 구조대가 찾았어요.
examples.en: The rescue team found the person who got lost in the jungle.

explain: 정글은 열대 지방의 나무가 빽빽한 숲이에요. 일반적인 숲은 '숲'이나 '산림'이라고 해서 달라요. '콘크리트 정글'처럼 도시를 빗대어 말할 때도 있어요.

phrases.example: 방학에 정글 탐험을 해 보고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to go on a jungle expedition during vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정글'과 자주 같이 쓰는 짝말로, 모험 이야기에 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing with 정글, often seen in adventure stories.

phrases.en: It is dangerous if you get lost in the jungle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 나타내는 '에서'와 함께 쓰는 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sentence pattern that uses 에서 to mark the place.
phrases.en_equiv: to get lost in the jungle

phrases.example: 서울은 높은 건물이 많아서 콘크리트 정글 같아요.
phrases.en: Seoul has many tall buildings, so it feels like a concrete jungle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 숲이 아니라 건물이 가득한 도시를 빗대어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is figurative and describes a city full of buildings, not a real jungle.

explain_en: 정글 is a dense tropical forest. An ordinary forest is '숲' or '산림', so they differ. It can also be used figuratively for a city, as in '콘크리트 정글'.

examples.en: A singing contest is being held at school.
My friend won a prize at a photo contest.
I also want to enter this contest.
The contest starts next Saturday.
I was busy preparing for the cooking contest.
There are many singers who became famous through contests.

explain: 비슷한 말로 '대회'가 있어요. 운동 경기에는 '대회'가 자연스럽고, 콘테스트는 노래, 요리, 사진처럼 솜씨를 겨루는 분야에 어울려요.

phrases.en: There is a cooking contest next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '콘테스트'와 비슷한 말이고, 운동 경기에도 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that also works naturally for sports events.

phrases.en: I want to enter the photo contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회에 참가한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to take part in a contest.

phrases.example: 동생이 노래 콘테스트에서 일 등 했어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling won first place in the singing contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the result.
phrases.en_equiv: to win first place in a contest

explain_en: A similar word is 대회. For sports, 대회 sounds more natural, while 콘테스트 fits skill-based fields like singing, cooking, and photography.

examples.en: The two countries become one.
The uniforms in our class are now uniform.
Once the opinions are unified, we start right away.

examples.ko: 글꼴이 통일된 발표 자료가 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: Presentation materials with a uniform font look good.
The method has not been unified yet.
I hope the method will be unified by next week.

explain: 한국에서는 남한과 북한의 '통일'이 큰 주제라서 뉴스에 자주 나와요. 표, 글꼴, 의견처럼 서로 달랐던 것이 하나로 맞춰질 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The students' opinions have not been unified yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 의견이나 규칙이 아직 하나가 아니라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means different opinions or rules are not yet made one.

phrases.en: I want to live in a unified country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '통일된'은 하나가 된 것을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes something that has become one.

phrases.example: 남북이 통일되면 기차로 유럽에 갈 수 있을 거예요.
phrases.en: If the two Koreas unify, we could go to Europe by train.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)면'을 붙여 앞으로의 일을 상상할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-(으)면' to imagine future possibilities.

explain_en: In Korea, the unification of South and North Korea is a big topic, so the word appears often in the news. It is also used when different tables, fonts or opinions are brought into line.
